title: attention-kernel-optimization-profiling-flashattention-paged-fused
content:
Summary:

This note captures the profiling experiments and observations for attention-kernel optimizations: FlashAttention variants, paged (KV-paging) attention, and fused QKV/attention ops. Goal was to identify latency and memory bottlenecks for causal transformer serving at production batch/sequence distributions and to produce actionable changes for the runtime kernel selection and rollout.

Key findings (high level):
- FlashAttention (Triton-based) gives best throughput for long sequences (>1024) on A100/RTX8000 with large batch sizes but has higher p99 tail when sequence length is variable due to kernel-launch overhead and workspace allocation.
- Paged attention (KV paging / chunked KV cache) reduces peak GPU memory for very long-context use-cases (8k+), but increases CPU/GPU synchronization cost and can hurt latency when cache fetches cross page boundaries.
- Fused ops (fusing QKV projections + attention + output projection into single CUDA/Triton kernel) reduce memory traffic and improve p50 by ~10-20% in microbenchmarks, but are brittle across model dims and require fallback paths for unsupported dims/seqs.

Experimental setup:
- Hardware: 1x NVIDIA A100 40GB (PCIe), 1x NVIDIA H100 (dev), 1x RTX 8000 (for repro).
- OS/Drivers: Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.1 (A100 tests used 11.8 for compatibility runs), cuBLAS 11.10, Triton 2.x (where applicable).
- Runtime: serving-runtime branch: attn-opt-experiments (PR #987). Python 3.10, PyTorch 2.1 for FlashAttention reference; custom C++/CUDA kernels built into runtime for fused variants.
- Models/profiles: GPT-like decoders only, hidden_dim 3072/4096, num_heads 32/64, head_dim 96. Sequences tested: 128, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192. Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8, 16. Warmup: 50 steps; measure next 200 steps.

Tools and commands used:
- nvprof/nsys for kernel timelines and SASS-level hotspots.
- nvtx ranges added around runtime phases (enqueue, batch-assemble, kernel-run, kv-copy).
- torch.cuda.memory_summary() and custom allocator logging for fragmentation checks.
- perf counters for DRAM throughput where possible.
- small microbench harness: tools/attn_bench.py (included in PR).

Representative results (microbenchmarks):
- Seq=512, batch=4, hidden=3072, A100:
  - baseline (cuBLAS matmul + naive softmax): tokens/s ~ 34k, p50 latency 27ms, p99 65ms, peak mem 12.3GB
  - FlashAttention (Triton impl): tokens/s ~ 47k (+38%), p50 19ms, p99 46ms, peak mem 10.1GB
  - Fused QKV+Attn (custom CUDA): tokens/s ~ 52k (+53%), p50 16ms, p99 40ms, peak mem 9.6GB
  - Paged-attn disabled (not beneficial at 512)

- Seq=4096, batch=1, hidden=4096, A100:
  - baseline: OOM or >38GB if using naive cache approach
  - FlashAttention (requires workspace): tokens/s ~ 6.2k, p50 198ms, p99 420ms, peak mem 36.8GB (workspace spikes)
  - Paged-attn (page_size 1024): tokens/s ~ 5.1k (-18% throughput vs Flash) but peak mem 20.5GB (fits into 40GB), p50 240ms, p99 520ms (cross-page sync cost)
  - Fused ops not yet implemented for 4096-dim model: engineering effort required

Observations and root causes:
- Workspace allocation: FlashAttention implementations often allocate a workspace per invocation; when sequence lengths vary, repeated alloc/free leads to fragmentation and kernel-launch stalls. Preallocating/reserving a per-worker max workspace reduced p99 by ~12% in experiments.
- Kernel launch overhead: Triton kernels have non-trivial launch latency for small batches and shorter seq lengths. The runtime should bias to cuBLAS/fused kernels for short sequences (<=256) and small batches to reduce tail latency.
- Memory copies for paged-attn: KV paging trades memory for additional copy and synchronization. Host pinned staging buffers and async memcpy help but don't eliminate cross-page boundary stalls. A two-tier async prefetch strategy (prefetch next N pages while generating current tokens) helped throughput by ~7% in the bench.
- Fused operators reduce global memory traffic (eliminate intermediate buffers) — biggest wins when model dims align well with warp/block sizes. However, maintenance burden increases (many dimension-specific kernels).

Integration notes for runtime kernel selector:
- Add runtime heuristics that consider: sequence length distribution, batch size, model hidden size, head dim, and model pinned to dedicated GPUs. Heuristics should pick between: fused-cuda, FlashAttention-Triton, cuBLAS (matmul), paged-attn enabled/disabled.
- Implement a per-worker preallocated workspace pool with configurable max_workspace_bytes per device and a LRU reuse policy. Metrics should expose workspace_utilization and allocation_rate.
- Expose page_size and prefetch_window for paged-attn in model config. Default page_size=1024 for A100; allow override for H100 tests.

Repro tips / commands used in bench:
- Run microbench on A100:
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python tools/attn_bench.py --model-dim 3072 --heads 32 --seq 512 --batch 4 --kernel flashattention --warmup 50 --steps 200 --profile nsys --out /tmp/attn_r1
- Collect timeline with nsight sys:
  nsys profile -t cuda,cudnn --output /tmp/attn_nsys ./run_bench.sh
- Memory fragmentation check (python):
  from torch import cuda
  print(cuda.memory_summary())

Open issues and TODOs:
- OOM risk for FlashAttention workspace on some model configs; need a guard to fall back to paged-attn or fused smaller kernels (SRV-ATTN-42).
- Fused kernel coverage: implement fused QKV+attn for hidden_dim 4096 + head_dim 128; track in GH PR #987.
- Paged-attn prefetching: prototype two-tier async prefetch and integrate into runtime scheduling to avoid cross-page stalls.
- Add end-to-end SLO tests in CI that simulate mixed sequence workloads (single token + long context interleaved) to catch p99 regressions introduced by kernel changes.

Action items (owners):
- Priya Patel: land per-worker workspace pool + metrics (SRV-ATTN-58) — ETA 2025-01-30
- David Lopez: prototype paged-attn prefetcher and evaluate with H100 (SRV-ATTN-61) — ETA 2025-02-10
- Michael Chen: implement heuristic policy for kernel selection and add integration tests for mixed sequences (SRV-ATTN-59) — ETA 2025-01-20
- Eng-sre: add nightly gate to run attn microbench across A100/H100 matrix to detect performance regressions (ticket: SRE-341)

Notes for rollout and risk mitigation:
- Feature flag fused kernels behind model-config and runtime flags. Canary to 5% of traffic with telemetry capturing p50/p90/p99 by seq-length bucket.
- For Dedicated customers, expose an "aggressive optimization" toggle (fused + flashattention) with warning about possible model dimensional incompatibilities and fallback behavior.

Appendix: quick checklist for further profiling cycles:
- Add NVTX ranges covering: batch-assemble, kv-fetch (paged), kernel-exec, kv-store.
- Track allocator fragmentation metrics and GC runs.
- Capture kernel occupancy reports for the fused kernels (nvprof --kernel-id).
- Test mixed-workload traces (chat + long-generation) with realistic interleaving to surface real-world p99 behavior.

Raw logs and perf artifacts are attached to the Confluence page listed in linked_artifacts.

End.
